sentences.text: Heard Sri Romeshwari Prasad, Advocate along with Mr. Krishna, learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. At the very outset, learned counsel for the applicants submitted that applicant no.2- Smt. Yashoda (mother-in-law of opposite party no.2) has been died and as such with regard to applicant no.2, the application under section 482 Cr.P.C. is dismissed as abated.

3. On the basis of several notices issued, appearance of Sri S.N. Singh, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 has been made, who preferred counter affidavit and the same has been replied by way of filing rejoinder affidavit on behalf of the applicants, but even in the revised call, none appeared on behalf of opposite party no.2.
4.

Considering the pendency of the instant matter, which is pending for last near about 14 years,
there is no option left but to proceed for final adjudication only on the basis of arguments raised by Harpal Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149818760/

5. The instant application under section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed to quash the entire proceedings of Case No. 7042 of 2009 (Minakshi vs. Ajai Singh and Others), arising out of Case Crime No.19 of 2003, under Section 498A I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Kavi Nagar,
District- Ghaziabad, pending in the court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.3, Ghaziabad.

sentences.text:
6. At the very outset, learned counsel for the applicants sought the attention of Court over the first information report lodged on behalf of the opposite party no.2, wherein the main allegation has been put forward against the husband and mother-in-law of the opposite party no.2 and rest of the other six persons being the close relative of the husband of opposite party no.2 has been implicated without any specific role assigned against them.
7.

Sri Krishna, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the applicants also submitted during pendency of the instant application divorce decree has been extended as ex-parte in favour of the opposite party no.2 and the same has never been put under challenge on behalf of the applicants, at present opposite party no.2 is residing as a married lady being the U.S. citizen.

8. It is also submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that during pendency of the instant application, husband and mother-in-law (applicant no.2 herein) of opposite party no.2 has already been expired and dates of their death have already been mentioned, which is available in the records.
9.

By bare perusal of the record, it is apparent that final report has already been preferred by concerned Investigating Officer under section 173 Cr.P.C. and the summoning order has been issued over the protest petition, which has been treated as complaint case by learned concerned court.

10. After hearing arguments raised by learned counsel for the applicants and by bare perusal of the record, it is crystal clear that the main allegation has been put forward against the husband and mother-in-law of the opposite party no.2, who have already been expired during pendency of the instant application and opposite party no.2 has already been granted divorce by the concerned court and at present, opposite party no.2 is residing in United States of America being a married lady and as a citizen of U.S. and rest of the other accused-applicants are having no specific role in connection to the allegation whatsoever has been put forward through F.I.R./complaint on behalf of the opposite party no.2.
11.

In view of the aforementioned facts and circumstances, the entire proceedings initiated against the applicant no.1 in shape of Case No. 7042 of 2009 (Minakshi vs. Ajai Singh and Others), arising out of Case Crime No.19 of 2003, under Section 498A I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Kavi Nagar, District- Ghaziabad, pending in the court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.3, Ghaziabad, is hereby quashed.
